name: Salu
overview: Salu was a male member of the tribe of Simeon, known primarily as the father of Zimri. His mention in Scripture is brief, with no additional notes or detailed background provided. His identity is anchored in his paternal relationship within the Simeonite lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Salu means "restored," which is a proper name but is not indicated as given directly by God. This meaning may reflect a theme of renewal or restoration, though the biblical text does not elaborate further on its significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Salu as a son of Simeon and as the father of Zimri. Beyond these two relationships, no other family connections are documented in the biblical record for Salu.
scriptureSignificance: Salu's significance in the biblical narrative stems from his role as the progenitor of Zimri, a figure mentioned in Numbers 25:14. Through this connection, Salu is part of the genealogical framework of the tribe of Simeon, contributing to the unfolding story of Israel's tribal history. Although Salu himself does not have a detailed narrative, his mention supports the lineage and tribal identity important in the Old Testament context.
